the cerebellum, as a phase-modulating device, supports the proper timing of learned responses, and the proper timing is a consequence of the proper causal relationship between cerebellar and motor neuronal activities.
the cerebellum, in addition to being the main timing device of the brain, also has the ability to generate causal relationships in the brain.
the cerebellar–MN network causality is a key determinant of the timing of the conditioned responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the timing of learned motor responses.
the causal relationships of cerebellar IPns and Mn during classical conditioning, and the role of these relationships in the generation of learned eyelid responses.
the timing of the generation of learned eyelid responses and the causal relationship between cerebellar and OO Mn firing activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cerebellar–OO Mn network is involved in proper timing of the learned eyelid response, and the IPns may be a neuronal phase-modulator of OO Mn activity, supporting the proper timing of the ongoing CRs.
IPns are involved in the timing of learned eyelid responses and that this timing depends on causal relations between the cerebellum and Mn.

the cerebellar–red nucleus–OO Mn network supports the proper timing of CRs as an emergent consequence of the proper timing of the causality of the learned response, which is supported by IPns firing activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cerebellum, through the IPns, is not only involved in the generation of learned eyelid responses, but also in the proper timing and causality of the responses.
the IPns and OO Mns may work together in a dynamic manner to generate the learned responses, but the IPns are not the sole cause of the CRs.
the cerebellum is involved in the proper generation of learned responses, but not in the proper timing, which would be the domain of the cerebellar–OO Mn network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cerebellum is involved in both the timing of motor events and in the causality of learned movements.
the IPns are involved in the proper performance of learned eyelid responses, which is in agreement with the cerebellar role as a neuronal phase-modulator.
the IPns are involved in the proper performance of learned CRs.
